sections: Source-guided rulings for an inexperienced host

decision: Automatically evaluate only represented source-backed normal ability-check mechanics after a trusted owner supplies die, applicable modifiers/proficiency and adjudicated DC. Choosing whether/how a check applies and its discretionary DC is separate human/source policy. Canonical permitted ruling inputs are structurally admitted only for current pending resolution/window/designated offered participant; admission is not authentication, rights, real mechanics or durable commit.
alternatives: Universal AI-created DC or prose-defined rule injection rejected: source discretion stays explicit.
Inventing public RulingRequest/Response or adding df-rules dependency rejected: this Design contract freezes examples of current boundaries without changing their public contracts.
Test-local arithmetic/pending state machine rejected: invoke existing actual resolver and canonical structural admission instead.
unresolved: Original stage is Design, not delivery of novice-host product flow. Test-only actual source mount is not reachable production composition.
Public RulingRequest/Response types, source-safe explanation projection, decline/wait/cancel/alternative producer semantics and absent/disconnected/unready host notices remain unresolved.
Full2024 source/catalog/rights denominator and source-qualified auto/discretion classification remain unresolved; SRD5.2.1 page6 normal-check subset only.

example_contract.automatic: Actual reviewed normal-check resolver compares supplied die11+ability2+proficiency2 against already adjudicated DC15: success; die10: failure. The resolver does not decide whether a check applies, set a DC, roll dice or produce durable state.
example_contract.discretion: Changing the trusted adjudicated DC15 to DC16 changes the same supplied total15 from success to failure; no human intervention is needed to perform the comparison, but source-discretionary choice of DC is not inferred.
example_contract.designated_ruling: Actual canonical HostCommand::ResolveRuling admission requires the exact pending resolution/window and offered participant/offer/option. Synthetic labels are opaque structural inputs, not implemented DC/decline/wait/cancel/alternative semantics.
example_contract.await_and_preservation: A participant without the offered adjudicator response receives typed UnofferedResponse; pending checkpoint, prior spent resource and prior ruling remain unchanged. No native absent-host policy, timeout or resume is run.
example_contract.scope: Test-only source mount of df-rules/src/ability_check.rs plus actual linked df-model APIs. Reuses the existing canonical interaction checkpoint fixture. This contract is not registered in a production native dispatcher.

failure_cases: Matching DC succeeds and one below fails; natural1/20 do not override comparison; invalid/missing draw or zero DC returns typed error without a fabricated answer.
An explicit pending Ruling accepts exactly an offered adjudicator/offer/option and rejects another participant, stale window, stale basis, wrong pending kind, unoffered option and zero limits.
Absent offered adjudicator returns canonical UnofferedResponse and unchanged pending checkpoint; no timeout, default draw/DC/resource spend or accepted ruling is invented.
Supplied checkpoint remains unchanged on successful structural admission and all refusals; already recorded spent resources/rulings remain intact.

integration_hooks.hook: Native contract auto-discovered by existing Cargo manifest; actual rules resolver source mounted only in this test target and actual canonical model admission linked through existing df-model dependency.

Production source-qualified automatic adjudication, authorized native RulingRequest/Response issuance, exact host binding/transfer, durable receipt lookup/once-only resume and cancellation remain unresolved; this test cannot supply those authorities.
